prompts: Investigate a production-style incident in this eShop source snapshot: a catalog item's price changes successfully, but a user's existing basket still displays the old price. Trace both versioned catalog update entrypoints through EF change tracking, the integration event/outbox transaction, RabbitMQ publication and dispatch, subscriber registration and consumer effects. Determine whether this repository actually implements the expected basket-price refresh, rather than assuming matching event names or interfaces prove it. Inspect the relevant services outside the Catalog project as needed using their source; do not run external databases, RabbitMQ, UI apps or deployment commands. Do not modify production code.

Produce an actionable repair and test plan. Explicitly separate local DB/outbox atomicity, publish status, message delivery/acknowledgement, deserialization/type registration, handler effects and basket/UI state. Identify failure modes that the current source handles or silently loses; avoid claiming guaranteed delivery, distributed atomicity or runtime success from static relationships. Save REPORT.json with findings [{id,statement,evidence:[{path,line}],certainty}] and testPlan. Use ids entrypoints, price-change, atomicity, routing, subscriptions, consumer-effect, basket, acknowledgement and remediation. Cite actual paths and symbols, including any project-scope limits.
